findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _walk (walk_error and the directory loop's _is_link call); README 'The coverage skip set and the walk' (the F2 sentence)
findings.finding: F2 is broader in the model than in the README and in Q-GOV-CAP's words ('an entry that vanished inside an any-depth skip directory ... everything else fails closed'). The directory loop passes _in_skip_directory(skip, rel + d), which includes the directory's own name, and walk_error tests the path of the directory being listed, so an any-depth skip directory that itself vanishes (ENOENT at its lstat or at its scandir) is also absent. Probe 3: ci/__pycache__ vanishing at lstat, or at scandir, passes; round 4 refused both. The code comment says so ('a skip directory that vanished while being walked'); the README does not. No gate effect: a directory that is gone holds nothing to classify and no link to judge, and a skip directory is never classified. Separately, the candidate test covers only the lstat branch; the walk_error branch (scandir ENOENT inside a skip directory, refusal outside one) has no test, though probe 3 shows it behaves as intended.
findings.requiredChange: Optional. Say in the README that an any-depth skip directory that vanished, or an entry inside one, is absent (or, if the owner wants the narrower reading, pass the parent path in both places), and add a test that substitutes os.scandir for a directory inside and outside a skip directory.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _walk and check_coverage (os.path.normpath); README walk paragraph ('the root is normalized first, F3')
findings.finding: F3 normalizes the root lexically with os.path.normpath and then walks the normalized root, not only tests it. Two spellings change meaning. (1) The empty string becomes '.', so check_coverage(doc, '') and tree_paths(doc, '') now walk and judge the current directory (probe 3: with a valid scratch tree as the working directory both pass) where round 4 refused the empty string as not an existing directory. (2) A root 'x/L/..' with L a link names the lexical parent x, while the file system resolves it to the parent of L's target (probe 3: the new model walks x, the round-4 model walked the target's parent). No gate effect for any current caller: the tests pass a computed repository path, Path('') already meant '.' under round 4, and whichever directory is walked is judged completely as the tree. The README sentence 'a root that is not an existing directory ... is refused' no longer holds for the string ''.
findings.requiredChange: Optional. Refuse an empty root (and, if wanted, a root with a '..' component) before normalizing, or use the normalized spelling only for the linked-root test, as Q-GOV-CAP's words say; or state the lexical normalization in the README.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _gate_link (target half: _matches(rel) and entry.startswith(rel + '/')); README F1 paragraph ('refused everywhere (..., the link rule)')
findings.finding: F1 reaches only the own-path half of the link rule. The target half locates the target by file identity and then compares its on-disk name with the record by spelling, so on a case-insensitive file system a data link to a case-variant directory that holds only skip-set files (or nothing) passes. Probe 2: a tree holding CI/__pycache__/x.cpython-312.pyc with docs/l -> ../CI, or docs/l -> ../CI/__pycache__/x.cpython-312.pyc, passes under both models, and the gate spelling ci/__pycache__/... then reads that content. Not added by this change, and no gate effect found: any non-skipped file under the variant spelling is refused by check_paths before the link rule runs, F1 makes pr_approvers refuse any PR adding such a path, and the exact gate spelling cannot exist beside it on that file system. The README's 'refused everywhere (..., the link rule)' reads naturally as the own path; the target bullet still says 'never by spelling'.
findings.requiredChange: Optional. In the target half also refuse when _case_variant(rel, classes, _resolve_spelling(rel, classes)) holds, and compare the ancestor test case-folded, so F1 holds in both halves.
